_fixture_meta.boundary: CALIBRATION -> PIPELINE/VIEWER (handbook Part X), RELATIVE branch
_fixture_meta.why_v0: The branch now exists (issue #15): src/relative_dsm.py takes a plain JPG/PNG, runs inference, normalizes to a unitless [0,1] height field and writes .npy + sidecar, with calibration skipped entirely. It stays v0 rather than v1 because Part IV item (c) - qualitative evaluation on genuinely non-georeferenced photographs - has not been done: the repo has no licence-clean sample images, and 'does the shape look right' is subjective evidence that belongs with Debopriya rather than a self-assessed pass. Automated coverage is real (tests/test_relative_dsm.py, 9 cases) but it is not the same claim.
_fixture_meta.owner: Nirmalya (handbook Part IV; role_cards/NIRMALYA.md starter task 2)

proposed_file.rationale: DepthWizard__Build_Guide.pdf section 10.1: a relative DSM is 'GeoTIFF if a spatial grid exists; otherwise NPY/PNG'. Here one does not exist.

array.meaning: internally shape-consistent only: taller reads as taller. No metres, no datum.

product.purpose: explicit discriminator; the metric fixture's counterpart

MUST_NOT_CARRY: any field implying a real-world map location

why_it_matters: The official PS requires it: plain JPG/PNG input with no spatial reference must still produce a relative DSM. Handbook Part IV is explicit that this is a genuinely separate requirement and that 'we can already produce relative depth' is NOT evidence the branch is finished.
scope_decision: Deferred, not forgotten. Issue #5 asks for the handoff to be wired and the two products kept distinct; it does not ask for the relative branch to be built, and the Day-1 rule caps this task at 'the smallest reliable handoff or contract'. Tracked as remaining Nirmalya lane work.
what_a_consumer_should_do_today: You may build against it, but treat it as v0: the field set can still change. Never compare a relative product against metric ground truth, and never convert one to the other without a real reference. The sidecar's product/units fields are the discriminator - check them.

normalization.why_percentile: min/max would let a single outlier pixel compress the whole scene into a sliver of the range and flatten the visible terrain. The bounds are recorded in the sidecar so the transform stays auditable and reversible.
normalization.degenerate_input: flat or non-finite input yields a valid flat field rather than inf/nan

depth_sign.meaning: +1 keeps the model's ordering; -1 inverts it
depth_sign.why_a_parameter: For NADIR imagery +1 is correct: DA2's output is disparity-like, and looking straight down closer to the camera means higher elevation - a rooftop is both nearer and taller. Confirmed by this repo's own measurements (zeroshot_3A_raw.json mean_corr +0.731/+0.694/+0.802; zeroshot_3B fitted a=+3.898). NOTE: scripts/05_zeroshot.py previously carried a comment claiming the opposite; it was never what the code did and has been corrected under this issue. For oblique or handheld input - which 'plain JPG/PNG' permits - the nadir argument collapses and the sign genuinely inverts, which is why this is a parameter and not a constant.

pseudo_gsd.why: heightfield_to_mesh() requires a gsd and has no default. A non-georeferenced image has no real GSD; passing a plausible metric value would smuggle a units claim into the mesh.

still_missing_for_v1: (c) qualitative evaluation on genuinely non-georeferenced photographs (needs licence-clean images; Debopriya stewards the evidence)
downstream consumer review of the sidecar field set (Ashmita/Aishee)
